{{Short description|Negatively-curved minimal surface}}
{{Use list-defined references|date=July 2025}}
{{CS1 config|mode=cs2}}
In [[differential geometry]], a '''Nadirashvili surface''' is an [[immersion (mathematics)|immersed]] complete bounded [[minimal surface]] in <math>\R^3</math> with negative [[Gaussian curvature]].  The first example of such a surface was constructed by {{Interlanguage link multi|Nikolai Nadirashvili|de|3=Nikolai Semjonowitsch Nadiraschwili}} in 1996. This simultaneously answered  a question of [[Jacques Hadamard|Hadamard]] about whether there was an immersed complete bounded  surface in <math>\R^3</math> with negative Gaussian curvature, and a question of [[Eugenio Calabi]] and [[Shing-Tung Yau]] about whether there was an immersed complete bounded minimal surface {{nowrap|in <math>\R^3</math>.<ref name=nadirashvili/>}}

{{harvtxt|Hilbert|1901}} showed that a complete immersed surface in <math>\R^3</math> cannot have constant negative Gaussian curvature,<ref name=hilbert/> and {{harvtxt|Efimov|1963}} show that the curvature cannot be bounded above by a negative constant.<ref name=efimov/> Therefore, Nadirashvili's surface necessarily has points where the Gaussian curvature is arbitrarily close {{nowrap|to 0.}} As a minimal surface, its [[mean curvature]] is 0 everywhere. Topologically, it is a disk. As an immersed surface, it intersects itself; it is not embedded. These self-intersections are necessary, as Colding and Minicozzi proved in 2008 that embedded complete bounded minimal disks do not exist.<ref name=colmin/>
